newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 2.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Police arrested a man yesterday in connection with Sunday night's axe attack on two Levin police officers. Page 1.

Television New Zealand has widened it influential final leaders' debate to include three potential National allies - ACT NZ, Christian Coalition and United. This has sparked accusations of political manipulation. Page 1.

A $40 million deal to settle an Opotiki Maori land grievance was signed in Wellington. Behind the platitudes of building true treaty partnerships, it seemed the government used the fear of political uncertainty in the MMP era to drive a hard bargain. Page 1.
A new free-to-air television channel is to be announced by TV3 today, an initiative of TV3's half-owner Canadian group Can West. Page 1.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger elaborated on his plans to consult other parties on the health sector, in an effort to put National on the front foot in the election campaign. He said the multi-party taskforce on retirement income could be used as a model for cross-party consensus on health. Page 2.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger attempted to put distance between himself and the Christain Coalition saying their extreme views were losing them support. Page 2.
Labour leader Helen Clark is emerging as the most likely candidate to be the next prime minister, Waikato university chancellor Bryan Gould said in yesterday's London Times newspaper. Page 2.

The June quarter had marked a significant turning point for manufacturing, but recovery from a "soft landing" would depend on how the Reserve Bank eased monetary conditions, the Manufacturers Federation said. Page 20.
Air New Zealand cemented its purchase of 49 percent of Ansett Australia with the signing of a commercial agreement at Sydney. Page 20.

Blue Star Group announced that it had acquired two more companies - Wellington Business Equipment and Auckland firm General Packaging - and a company official said the group was looking to buy more. Blue Star, owned by United States Offices Products, has expanded agreesively in New Zealand. Page 20.

Australia's biggest retailer, Cole Myers said its net profit fell 33.8 percent to NZ$325.21 million in the year ended July 28 as earnings at its Kmart discount chain and its department stores slumped. Page 20.

Hotel operators could be heading for a price-cutting war as the industry tries to fill hundreds of rooms planned for construction in the next two years, according to the Standard and Poor's tourism industry profile. Page 21.
New Zealand First Leader Winston Peters confirmed he would introduce legislation to buy back Forestry Corporation as a priority when parliament resumes.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger continued to promote his calls for a post-election dialogue on health, despite receiving a chilly response from other parties on the idea.
Brierley Investments had raised 20 billion yen (NZ$257 million) through a 10-year private placement by Japanese insurance companies. Page 28.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Social Welfare admits it made mistakes in its dealings with an infant girl who was beaten to death by her father. Page 1.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger distanced himself from the Christian Coalition on the same day a poll showed his supporters do not a bar of the Christians.

Supermarket operator Progressive Enterprises' profit plunge in the July year has left it in breach of the conditions of its bank loans. Under its banking covenants, earnings before interest and tax needed to be at least two times its annual interest charge.
Air New Zealand and News Ltd yesterday formalised the agreement by which the New Zealand carrier becomes the joint owner of Ansett Australia.

The 800 cents a share being offered to small Power New Zealand shareholders by both Mercury Energy and Utilicorp New Zealand respresents a significant premium to fair value, an independent appraisal by merchant bank Bancorp has found.
Auckland-based farm equipment group Tru-Test Ltd expects to list on the stock exchange in a few years as part of an anticipated rationalisation of the agri-tech industry.
Westpac New Zealand's tax-paid earnings dropped 27 percent to $29.4 million in the June quarter, despite the inclusion of five weeks' trading from newly-acquired Trust Bank.
